sentences.text:
This petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India has been preferred by petitioner being aggrieved by the impugned order dated 03.12.2025 passed in Regular Civil Appeal No.151/2025 by Principal District Judge, Gwalior and Appellate Tribunal under Food Safety and Standards Act,
whereby Appellate Court has rejected the application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act preferred by petitioner.
2. Brief facts of the case are that the Food Safety Officer inspected the petitioner's firm, where the petitioner was found present and operating the business.

During inspection, various food articles such as mixed milk, skimmed curd, ghee, and paneer, which were being used for preparation and sale for human consumption at the premises, were found stored in the shop.
On inspection, the said articles were found to be sub-standard and misbranded.
Accordingly, samples were taken and sent for analysis to the Public Analyst, Bhopal, who submitted a report wherein some of the samples were found to be misbranded.

3. Thereafter, the Food Safety Officer filed a private complaint before the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11289 2 MP-1936-2026 Adjudicating Officer, who issued a show-cause notice to the petitioner.
The petitioner filed his reply denying the allegations.

After recording evidence, a penalty of Rs.2,00,000/- was imposed upon the petitioner under Section 51 of the Food Safety and Neelesh Chaubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101726120/

sentences.text: 4. Being aggrieved by the said order dated 28.11.2024, the petitioner preferred an appeal before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal along with an application for condonation of delay under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.

The Appellate Tribunal, after hearing learned counsel for both the parties,
rejected the application for condonation of delay.

5. Aggrieved by the impugned order of the Appellate Tribunal, the petitioner has filed the present petition contending that the impugned order is not in consonance with the spirit of law and that the appeal ought not to have been dismissed solely on the ground of limitation.

It is submitted that sufficient cause was shown for condonation of delay by stating that the copy of the impugned order dated 28.11.2024 was received on 05.12.2024, and thereafter the petitioner contacted his counsel,
and the appeal was filed on 28.01.2025.
Thus, the delay of near about 25 days is bona fide and inadvertent.
Hence, prayer has been made for setting aside the impugned order.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State supported the impugned order and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
8.

According to Rule 3.3.1 Food Safety and Standards Act:-
Every appeal under Section 70 of the Act arising out of a decision of the Adjudicating Officer appointed under Section 68 of the Act, shall be filed within a period of 30 days from the date on which the copy of the order against which the appeal is filed, is received by the appellant.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11289 3 MP-1936-2026 Provided,
however, that the Appellate Tribunal may allow a maximum of another 30 days to entertain an appeal if it is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing the appeal within first 30 days.
9.

So, on perusal of Rule 3.3.1 of Food Safety and Standards Act, it is clear that appeal must be filed within thirty days and next thirty days must be condoned by the Appellate Tribunal if appellant shows sufficient cause for not filing the appeal on time.
10. In the present case, the copy of the order was received by the petitioner on 05.12.2024, and the appeal was filed on 28.01.2025.
Thus, the delay is of near about 25 days, which is well within the condonable period prescribed under the Rules.

11. The Apex Court in the case of N.Balakrishnan Vs. M. Krishnamurthy (1998) 7 SCC 123 in Para 10 and 11 has held as under:-
10.

sentences.text: The primary function of a court is to adjudicate the dispute between the parties and to advance substantial justice.
The time- limit fixed for approaching the court in different situations is not because on the expiry of such time a bad cause would transform into a good cause.
11. Rules of limitation are not meant to destroy the rights of parties.
They are meant to see that parties do not resort to dilatory tactics, but seek their remedy promptly.
The object of providing a legal remedy is to repair the damage caused by reason of legal injury.
The law of limitation fixes a lifespan for such legal remedy for the redress of the legal injury so suffered.
Time is precious and wasted time would never revisit.
During the efflux of time, newer causes would sprout up necessitating newer persons to seek legal remedy by approaching the courts.
So a lifespan must be fixed for each remedy.
Unending period for launching the remedy may lead to unending uncertainty and consequential anarchy.
The law of limitation is thus founded on public policy.

It is enshrined in the maxim interest reipublicae up sit finis litium (it is for the general welfare that a period be put to lititgation).
12.
So, in view of the law laid down by Apex Court in the aforesaid case, it is clear that rule of limitation are not meant to destroy the substantive right of the parties.
The right of filing an appeal in terms of provisions of Act of 2006 is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11289 4 MP-1936-2026 statutory right of the present petitioner.
Even otherwise, the delay was also not inordinate.
Therefore, the Tribunal ought to have resorted to a lenient approach in the present case and ought to have allowed the application for condonation of delay.
Therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court, Appellate Court has committed an error in not condoning the delay which is just 25 days.

13. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, in the interest of justice, the delay assigned by petitioner in filing the appeal before the Appellate Authority is bona fide in nature, therefore, the only delay of 25 days in filing the appeal by the petitioner deserves to be and is hereby condoned.

The impugned order passed by Appellate Authority is set aside and the matter is remanded to the Appellate Authority to decide the appeal afresh on merits in accordance with law after giving opportunities of hearing to both the parties.
14. Accordingly, petition stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
